What it means: The Boston City Council Committee on Ways and Means held a virtual hearing on November 18, 2026 [06:04, 06:28], regarding Dockets 2080 and 2081 [07:25, 07:27, 07:57]. These dockets propose transferring $787,501 from the city reserve for collective bargaining to the Boston Public Schools department for fiscal year 2027 [07:29, 07:38, 08:00, 08:07]. The supplemental appropriation covers a one-year contract extension for roughly 475 custodians represented by Local Union 1952 International Union of Painters and Allied Trades District Council 35 [07:45, 07:54, 08:28, 11:27, 15:14]. The contract provisions include a 2 percent base wage increase alongside a flat $800 salary addition beginning in September 2026 [08:34, 08:40, 11:28, 11:30].

Who moved it: Mayor Michelle Wu sponsored the orders, which were referred to the committee on November 4, 2026 [08:44, 08:47], following an October 14, 2026 vote by the Boston School Committee to approve the appropriations [08:56]. Ways and Means Chair Ben Weber presided over the hearing [05:56, 05:59], which included testimony from City Budget Director Jim Williamson [09:16, 10:04] and BPS Director of Labor Relations Jeremiah Hasson [09:19, 10:07]. City Councilors Flynn and Mejia attended and voiced support for the custodians and the agreement [09:13, 09:40, 12:51, 14:19].

What to watch: City officials respectfully requested that the City Council pass the orders during a separate council meeting so the wage adjustments can be implemented retroactively [10:19, 10:22, 11:41, 12:17]. No public testimony was offered during the hearing [22:59, 23:00], and Chair Weber adjourned the session [23:33, 23:35]. The transcript does not settle whether or when the full City Council subsequently voted to approve the contract funding [09:01, 10:22].

summary: On November 18, 2026, Committee Chair Ben Weber convened a virtual hearing [05:56] on Docket Numbers 2080 and 2081 [07:25] to discuss reducing the reserve for collective bargaining by $787,501 to fund a one-year contract extension for Boston Public Schools custodians represented by Local Union 1952 Painters and Allied Trades District Council 35 [07:28], [08:00]. City Budget Director Jim Williamson and BPS Labor Relations Director Jeremiah Hasson explained that the contract includes a 2% base wage increase and an $800 flat addition to annual salaries starting September 2026 [08:34], [10:05], [11:28]. Councilors Flynn and Mejia expressed support for the funding and praised the work of school custodians [12:51], [14:19]. No public testimony was submitted [23:00], and the chair adjourned the hearing without a vote [23:33].
